title: views: rows escaping an updatable view, a view running as its owner or its caller, and a materialized view going stale

steps.note: products, and two views of the cheap ones: one plain, one WITH CHECK OPTION.
through the plain view, insert a product at 30.00. the view's WHERE says under 10, and nothing stops it.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, price FROM cheap ORDER BY id
steps.note: the row went into products, and the view can't see what it just inserted.
the same insert through the checked view: the new row would be invisible to the view, so it's refused.

error.message: new row violates check option for view "cheap_checked"

steps.sql: UPDATE cheap_checked SET price = 15.00 WHERE id = 1
steps.note: and an UPDATE that would push a row out of the view is refused too.

error.message: new row violates check option for view "cheap_checked"

steps.note: a role that may read a view of products, but not products itself.

steps.sql:
SET ROLE views_clerk;
SELECT name, price FROM price_list ORDER BY name
steps.note: as the clerk, the default view: it reads products with its owner's rights, so it works.

steps.sql: SELECT name, price FROM price_list_invoker ORDER BY name
steps.note: the security_invoker view checks the clerk's own rights on products, and the clerk has none.
back to the owner. a materialized view of revenue per product, from order lines.
a new order comes in: three teapots.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, revenue FROM revenue ORDER BY id
steps.note: the materialized view still shows what was true when it was built. no teapot.

steps.sql:
SELECT p.id, p.name, sum(l.qty * p.price) AS revenue
FROM products AS p JOIN order_lines AS l ON l.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY p.id
steps.note: the same query, live, sees it.
REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY needs a unique index to match old rows to new ones, and there isn't one.

steps.sql:
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON revenue (id);
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY revenue
steps.note: with a unique index on id, the concurrent refresh works: readers keep the old rows until it commits.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, revenue FROM revenue ORDER BY id
